text:
olivia: Quick signal — nightly serving cluster after the kernel-switch commit shows higher batch growth and repeated workspace OOMs during steady traffic. Repro'd locally on a dedicated rig with the same traffic profile. Sharing top-line profiler snippets and tentative root causes.

rajesh: Can you paste the flame/top allocations? My guess: kernel picked a variant that increases pad/stride or forces larger workspace per sequence, so effective per-seq overhead rose. Could be KV cache shadowing too.

olivia: Paste from local run:
```
[batcher] effective_batch_growth = 1.8x
[mem] workspace_alloc_peak: 12.3GB -> 18.1GB
p95_latency: 48ms -> 93ms
OOMs: 3 in 30m (workspace OOM)
kernel_selected: fused-attn-v2 (auto)
previous_kernel: attn-legacy
pad_median_per_seq: 1.2kB -> 3.6kB
kv_shadow_reclaims: +220 per min
```

maria: fused-attn-v2 is known to increase pad alignment (larger tile sizes). First quick checks: measure pad distribution (histogram of pad bytes per sequence) and force the legacy kernel to compare. Try `FORCE_KERNEL=attn-legacy` for a control run.

olivia: Did that — forcing legacy drops peak memory ~22% and p95 back to ~52ms. Reproducer command I used:
```
./infra/bench/run_micro.sh --model llama-13b --seq-lens "16,64,256" --batch-size 16 --profile --dump=pads.json
```

zach: Two angles: allocator and batching heuristics. Allocator: our current min_slab is 256KB which multiplies pad inefficiency into big workspace waste for many small sequences. Quick experiment: lower min_slab to 64KB (flag `allocator.min_slab=64KB`) — could reduce wasted slack but may increase fragmentation. Worth trying on canary.

rajesh: Also instrument `pad_entropy` and `pad_skew` metrics (histograms) and expose `kv_shadow_hits` / `kv_shadow_reclaims`. We should gate an automatic fallback: if pad_entropy > 0.6 and workspace_growth_rate > 1.5x, fall back to attn-legacy or force smaller batcher target.

maria: Agreed. We should avoid long-term allocator changes without collecting fragmentation signal (`slab_fragmentation_ratio`). If fragmentation increases beyond 0.25 after 24h, revert.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled back `kernel-switch` on canary cluster (canary-3) at 03:14 UTC — automatic rollback triggered by workspace OOM alerting.

olivia: I'll open a short PR with: 1) two new metrics (pad_hist, pad_entropy) + dashboard, 2) an allocator flag to try 64KB min_slab behind a runtime flag, and 3) a canary config to auto-fallback kernel on pad_entropy threshold. I'll run a 24h canary and post results.

rajesh: When you open the PR, include a small reproducer (the bench script) and a before/after table with peak mem and p95. Also add a test that asserts batcher growth < 1.5x for the sample load.

maria: :thumbsup:

zach: If the allocator flag helps, we should follow up with an enhanced compaction pass (lazy-defrag) to reclaim fragmentation risk. Otherwise we can add a cheap heuristic: tighten continuous-batching growth when average pad_per_seq > threshold.

olivia: ACK. I'll paste the pads.json dump and initial dashboard once PR is up. Thanks all.
